I've always been dismissive of the concept of "throw a big name at a movie and it will do better" but I could never quite figure out the cause and effect involved, until I had an epiphany:

Really big name actors aren't just great actors - they also have a talent for making movies. What this means is that they can read a script and figure out if it's worth being in the film. They can look at the director and costars and decide if it's worth auditioning. So they serve as a filter for movies worth seeing. I'd love to go back through movie production histories and see how often a big name actor leaves a movie or "runs into a scheduling conflict" when the director leaves - I'll bet it's a pretty high percentage.

On top of that, there's the self-fulfilling prophecy that when a production company lands a big-name actor for a movie, they pour far more marketing muscle into it.

But suits in production companies don't get that - they think it's "put Will Smith on the poster and people come to see the movie"
